results.content: With three months to go until the U.S. midterm elections in November, voters increasingly seem to prefer Democrats over the Republican Party that has had control of Congress for the last two years. Results of a Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday showed that 42% of registered voters would vote for a Democratic congressional candidate at present, compared to 37% for a Republican. The same survey also found that, for the first time in nearly a decade of its polling series, voters perceive the Democratic Party as having a better plan for the economy than the Republican Party. results.content: Months of immigration enforcement controversies have taken their toll, and new polling shows it could be a problem for Republicans heading into the midterms. About eight in 10 independent voters say U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has used too much force in its nationwide operations, according to a poll from YouGov, which sampled 1,000 voters in late July. An earlier YouGov poll, which was conducted before the two shootings, found that most independents – 62% – believe ICE has gone too far. results.content: One in five Republicans say their finances are worse after year and a half of Trump. Americans broadly believe that the economy is growing worse under President Donald Trump’s stewardship and say that they are personally worse off after a year and a half of his second presidency. Roughly 53 percent of all registered voters, including nearly 25 percent of Republicans, said they were in a worse position now, as the war with Iran and other issues continue to drive up consumer costs, including the price of fuel.
